To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that

e-government is an important source of public value creation and the critical factors that can be used to evaluate the public value of Sri Lankan e-government are quality of public information, functionalities of electronic service delivery, provision of information services through e-enabled counter, user orientation of service delivery, improving organizational efficiency, openness and response of e-government, enhancing trust, achieving social equity and environmental sustainability.

the quality of public online information, functionalities of electronic public services, user orientation of service delivery, and openness and responsiveness of government are the key critical factors for evaluating public value of e-Government.
quality of public information, functionality of e-services, e-enabled counters, and user orientation are the critical factors for assessing the public value of the e-government.
In summary, our research is concerned with
identifying the critical factors to evaluate the public value of government websites in Sri Lanka.
the public value of the e-government in Sri lanka.
the public value of government and the role of information and communication technologies in creating that value.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that

the public value of the e-goverment can be evaluated by the extent of quality public information online, the functionalities of electronic services provided by the government, the provision of information and service through e-enabled counters of the government, the user orientation of public services, improving organisational eficiency, openness and responsiveness of the government, enhancing trust in the government, ensuring confidentiality of citizen’s information, achieving social equality, and environmental sustainability.

the public value of the e-government can be evaluated by considering both the internal (i.e. quality of information and services) and the external (i.e. openness, responsiveness, trust, equity, sustainability) factors.
the quality of public value is a function of both the quality of the public information and the quality of the services provided by the e-government.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
e-government can create public value in a variety of ways.

the public value of the e-government can be evaluated based on the quality of public service delivery through e-enabled counters and electronic services, the quality of public services online, and the quality of the information provided online.
the quality of e-government initiatives is critical for creating public value.
The main takeaway from our work is that
the critical factors for assessing the public value of government are different from the critical factors for achieving e-government maturity.
the quality of public services and the quality of public service delivery is the key to evaluating the public value creation of e-government.

the public value of an e-government initiative is determined by the extent to which it is able to deliver a set of benefits that are valued by the citizens, and that these benefits can only be realised when the critical factors are properly considered.
